t.1.129.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Seeing Bhīmasena surpassing all in strength and Dhanaṃjaya accomplished in learning, the evil-minded Duryodhana was consumed with anguish.
t.1.129.2: Then Karṇa Vaikartana and Śakuni Saubala too sought, by many means, to kill those Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.129.3: And the Pāṇḍavas too, those tamers of foes, knew all of it, yet, abiding by Vidura's counsel, they did not bring it into the open.
t.1.129.4: Then the citizens, seeing the sons of Pāṇḍu endowed with virtues, gathered together and spoke of them in the squares and in the assembly halls.
t.1.129.5: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, lord of the people, whose eyes are wisdom, did not obtain the kingdom before because of his blindness; how then could he become king?
t.1.129.6: Likewise Bhīṣma Śāṃtanava, true to his word and great in his vow, having renounced the kingdom long ago, will never take it now.
t.1.129.7: Therefore let us today duly consecrate the eldest Pāṇḍava, who, though young, has the conduct of the old, who is truthful and knows compassion.
t.1.129.9: Hearing those words of theirs as they spoke, those people devoted to Yudhiṣṭhira, the evil-minded Duryodhana burned with anguish.
t.1.129.8: For he, the knower of dharma, will honor Bhīṣma Śāṃtanava and Dhṛtarāṣṭra together with his sons, and will provide them with enjoyments of every kind.
t.1.129.10: Tormented, that evil-minded one could not endure their words, and, burning with jealousy, he went to Dhṛtarāṣṭra.
t.1.129.12: Father, I have heard the inauspicious words of the townspeople as they chatter: disregarding you and Bhīṣma, they want the Pāṇḍava as their lord.
t.1.129.11: Then, seeing his father alone, he paid him honor; tormented by the citizens' affection for the Pāṇḍavas, he afterwards spoke these words.
t.1.129.14: Formerly Pāṇḍu obtained the kingdom from his father by virtue of his own merits; you too, though the kingdom had come to you, did not receive it, because of your lack of qualities.
t.1.129.13: And this is Bhīṣma's view as well, for he does not desire the kingdom. But the people in the city wish to cause us the greatest distress.
t.1.129.16: Thus we, together with our sons, deprived of the royal line, shall become despised by the world, O lord of the earth.
t.1.129.15: If this Pāṇḍava obtains Pāṇḍu's inheritance, then surely his son will receive it in turn, and after him another, his son's son, and so on from one to the next.
t.1.129.17: O king, quickly arrange things so that we may not, living on the food of others, forever fall into hell.
t.1.129.18: For if you, O king, had once been firmly established in the kingship, we too would surely have obtained the kingdom, even though the people were unwilling.
